items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: Then Manuel Perez told me about Eddie Garland.

ctx.x: I just told you, he was the best player that I've ever heard in my life.

The world's greatest worst. Really? The world's greatest worst? Yeah. The world's greatest worst? Yeah. The world's greatest worst? Worth. Then Manuel Perez told me about Eddie Garland. He was playing at the Dixon Park two bands. Oh, yeah. And I told him I hadn't even known of a good bass player. He said, yeah, I know a guy driving the barrel wagon, Eddie Garland. He used to phone them. He used to phone them, I called. He was driving a what? A barrel wagon, the whole empty barrel of wine and whiskey. Oh, is that…

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: He was working in Storoville quite a while with Manuel Perez.

ctx.x: Well, just one second. I was going to ask, I'll finish up to the Henry Martin business. How come he wasn't with you? Did he live long or was he dead by that time?
He was working in Storoville quite a while with Manuel Perez. He worked with me when, you know, he was on there one night, you see.
Yeah, I wonder why you didn't want to take him to California too.
